args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The service was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it, and check why it was promoted even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

- **What went wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. The test version of v2.3.1 had also been failing health checks in staging.
- **Rollback:** I picked v2.3.0 because it's the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before, it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It says what failed, what I rolled back and the result. It also lists next steps: find why v2.3.1 broke before deploying it again, and find out how it reached production even though it failed in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
